incidents.victim: Country-code TLD registrars (.as American Samoa, .gh Ghana, .sl Sierra Leone)
incidents.vector: Attackers hijacked DNS records for three national ccTLD registries by passing domain ownership checks, then obtained valid HTTPS certificates for targeted domains.
incidents.impact: DNS resolution subverted across three ccTLD namespaces; Google and other organizations' services targeted; valid TLS certificates issued to attacker-controlled domains enabling potential traffic interception.

incidents.victim: IDC Frontier Cloud (Japanese government cloud infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against cloud service provider hosting Japanese government workloads; specific entry vector not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Server infrastructure disrupted across IDC Frontier Cloud environment; Japanese government services dependent on the platform impacted.

incidents.victim: Yandex (Russian cloud, search, and internet services) — three data centers
incidents.attacker: Ukraine — military operations (retaliation for Russian infrastructure strikes)
incidents.vector: Ukrainian drones struck three Yandex data centers in Ryazan, Kaluga, and Vladimir regions over four days; physical destruction used as a cyber-disruption vector against commercial and government cloud infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Approximately 80 Yandex cloud services disrupted; two of six data centers fully shut down; ~64,000 cloud customers affected including retailers, telecoms, TikTok Russia, and payment services. Cloudflare observed a 50% drop in automated bot traffic from Russia following the strikes.

incidents.victim: Nikkei (Japanese financial media group)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Nikkei's Google Workspace environment in July 2026 via undisclosed means; second breach of Nikkei reported this year.
incidents.impact: Extent of data exposure under investigation; access to Nikkei's corporate productivity and communications environment. Disclosure came months after the July intrusion.

incidents.victim: French supermarket chains — hundreds of locations
incidents.vector: Cyberattack targeting refrigeration control systems across hundreds of French supermarket locations; attack vector not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Refrigeration systems disrupted across hundreds of French stores creating food safety risk; financial losses under assessment.

incidents.victim: FBI (US Federal Bureau of Investigation) — agent personnel records
incidents.vector: Exploited an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability (CVE-2026-35273) on the FBI's contractor-managed recruitment portal; Accenture, the FBI's contractor, had failed to apply available security patches.
incidents.impact: Personal and professional data of nearly all FBI special agents stolen — including names, unit assignments, medical and psychiatric records, and specialization details. FBI terminated Accenture as a contractor. Three ShinyHunters suspects arrested: a Canadian cybersecurity executive and co-founder of Cypfer (Edward Dubrovsky) in Pennsylvania, a Dutch national (Pepijn van der Stap) in the Netherlands, and a Jordanian teenager in Jordan.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect and Prisma Access VPN
incidents.vector: Authentication bypass in Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect and Prisma Access (CVE-2026-0257) exploited by ransomware actors to open unauthorized VPN sessions without valid credentials.
incidents.impact: Ransomware actors gaining unauthorized network entry via VPN bypass on unpatched Palo Alto appliances globally; patches available but exploitation active. All organizations with exposed PAN-OS GlobalProtect should patch immediately.

incidents.victim: Global critical infrastructure — US government, manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, education, and targets in Southeast Asia, Africa
incidents.attacker: China — state-linked espionage group (Integrity Technology Group contractor)
incidents.vector: Integrity Technology Group, a Beijing-based company with documented Chinese government ties, provides enabling tooling: EBurst password spraying against Office 365, MicroScan (1,300+ vulnerability scripts), SoftEther VPN persistence, and XSS credential harvesting; attackers combine automated scanning with hands-on intrusion using LOTL techniques.
incidents.impact: Confirmed compromise of US government, critical manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, and education targets; campaign active since at least 2021 and ongoing. Joint advisory AA26-281A issued by 11 agencies across 6 countries (US CISA/FBI/NSA, UK NCSC, Australia ACSC, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, Spain). UK previously sanctioned Integrity Technology Group.

incidents.victim: ASOS (UK online clothing retailer)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to ASOS customer platform used to send a mass push notification to all customers; attacker gained access to customer data through undisclosed means.
incidents.impact: Names and contact details of all ASOS customers accessed; payment card information and passwords not believed affected. UK NCSC published guidance for affected customers.

incidents.victim: Oracle Health (legacy Cerner EHR platform) — 20 million patients
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Oracle Health's legacy Cerner electronic health record environment; breach occurred approximately one year before disclosure.
incidents.impact: Health records for approximately 20 million patients compromised. Oracle disclosed the full patient count roughly one year after the breach occurred, raising significant concerns about the adequacy and timeliness of breach notification.

incidents.victim: Osaka Metropolitan University
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against university IT network; specific initial access vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: University IT network disrupted; classes canceled; academic operations suspended pending investigation and recovery.

incidents.victim: KillSec ransomware group — law enforcement action
incidents.vector: N/A — law enforcement takedown across four European countries.
incidents.impact: European authorities dismantled KillSec ransomware group; seized servers, conducted house searches in four countries; arrested three members including a 16-year-old Romanian national in Spain identified as the main administrator, a Dutch national (Fouad Eltibrizi) arrested in the UK, and a third suspect in Romania. The US filed extradition requests for Eltibrizi.

incidents.victim: Denmark — central population register (CPR database), 8.8 million citizens
incidents.vector: Attacker accessed Denmark's central population register through a privileged administrative account protected only by the password '123456' with no multi-factor authentication enforced.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses, and CPR social security numbers of all 8.8 million Danish citizens — living and deceased — stolen; data scale enables national-level identity fraud and targeted phishing operations.

incidents.victim: ATNS (Air Traffic and Navigation Services) — South Africa air traffic control
incidents.vector: Ransomware-linked malware deployed against ATNS operational technology (OT) network; attack thwarted before disrupting live air traffic control operations.
incidents.impact: Attack could have disrupted air traffic operations at South African airports including Port Elizabeth; thwarted before full deployment. South Africa issued an RFQ for forensic incident response services; incident highlights critical OT exposure in aviation sector.

incidents.victim: Water utilities, telecom providers, regional governments, and universities — Spain and Portugal
incidents.vector: Warlock ransomware deployed simultaneously across multiple Spanish and Portuguese-speaking critical sector organizations via undisclosed initial access vector.
incidents.impact: Ransomware-encrypted systems across water utility, telecommunications, regional government, and higher education organizations in Spain and Portugal; operations disrupted, data potentially exfiltrated.

incidents.victim: Multiple South Korean banks and financial institutions
incidents.vector: Attacker used ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration testing framework incorporating multiple LLMs (DeepSeek, GLM, Grok), to autonomously identify and exploit vulnerabilities; used Claude agents to conduct sessions resembling legitimate API usage to evade detection.
incidents.impact: Confirmed data exfiltration from multiple South Korean banks; loan origination systems, employee workstations, and customer data repositories accessed. South Korean authorities launched an investigation. First confirmed use of AI-native tooling in large-scale financial sector intrusions.

incidents.victim: iRhythm Technologies (cardiac monitoring device manufacturer) — 360,000 patients
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to iRhythm patient data systems in June 2026; method of intrusion not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: 360,000 patient records stolen including cardiac monitoring data and personal health information; disclosed to affected patients months after the June 2026 breach.

incidents.victim: US financial institutions — ATM networks (1,500+ attacks)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financial fraud (Tren de Aragua, Venezuelan organized crime)
incidents.vector: Tren de Aragua criminal organization deployed ATM jackpotting malware against US bank ATM networks, causing machines to dispense all available cash to waiting operatives.
incidents.impact: $40.73 million stolen from US financial institutions via 1,500+ ATM jackpotting attacks; US Treasury sanctioned 10 network members on September 30, 2026. Group was previously designated as a Foreign Terrorist Organization.

incidents.victim: Government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, Philippines, and Cambodia
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails delivering the Antino backdoor to government and policy targets across Southeast and East Asia; campaign tracks regional diplomatic and policy developments.
incidents.impact: Persistent backdoor access established within government and policy environments across four countries; ongoing intelligence collection on regional geopolitical positions.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government-affiliated AI research organizations
incidents.vector: AI-assisted spear-phishing using AI policy event lures to deliver real-time adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) pages, harvesting researcher credentials and session tokens.
incidents.impact: Credential and session token theft from Taiwan government-affiliated AI research organizations; persistent access likely established for intelligence collection on AI policy positions.

incidents.victim: US Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC) — 3 million DoD personnel records
incidents.vector: Unauthorized actors gained access to a DMDC file-sharing server and maintained access undetected for approximately nine months before discovery.
incidents.impact: Personal data of approximately 3 million current and former US military personnel and DoD civilians exposed, including records held by the agency responsible for maintaining Pentagon personnel files.

incidents.victim: US financial institutions — sanctioned criminal network (A7 Network)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — sanctions evasion network supporting ransomware
incidents.vector: A7 Network operated as an Iran- and Russia-linked sanctions evasion network that also provided financial services and infrastructure to ransomware operators and other cybercriminals.
incidents.impact: US Treasury designated the A7 Network on October 1, 2026, exposing a financial infrastructure layer that enabled both state-aligned sanctions evasion and criminal ransomware payments to move money internationally.

incidents.victim: Organizations globally using Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
incidents.vector: Three zero-days: CVE-2026-88771/88772 (unauthenticated RCE, CVSS 9.5) exploited since September 3 before patch availability on September 27; CVE-2026-88779 (SAML authentication bypass, DoS/exploitation) disclosed October 3; CVE-2026-107406 (memory overflow RCE/DoS in SAML SP/IdP) disclosed October 9.
incidents.impact: 50,277+ internet-exposed NetScaler instances identified; web shells deployed across dozens of organizations in government, financial services, healthcare, and technology. Australian organizations confirmed affected. Three distinct zero-days in the same product family within two weeks.

incidents.victim: Open-source ecosystem — npm Axios HTTP client, Mastra AI framework, Rust arrayref crate
incidents.vector: North Korea-affiliated actors injected malicious code into three widely-used open-source packages with Web3-based command-and-control infrastructure; the ChainDrop worm propagated the payload to 400+ downstream npm packages.
incidents.impact: Cloud credentials, API keys, and environment variables exfiltrated from developer build pipelines. 400+ npm packages infected downstream. Organizations that ran affected versions should treat all secrets present in build environments as compromised.

incidents.victim: Financial services organizations (multiple, targeted globally)
incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering: target tricked by a fake video conferencing application prompt that copied and executed a malicious PowerShell command, deploying GeniexLoader which installed GeniexRAT for persistent remote access.
incidents.impact: GeniexRAT remote access trojan deployed on victim endpoints; enables credential theft, lateral movement, and financial system compromise. Consistent with North Korea's ongoing campaign targeting the global financial sector.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government and diaspora organizations (employees in France, US, and Canada)
incidents.vector: ClickFix technique using fake CAPTCHA prompts embedded in compromised Ukrainian government websites; pages copied a malicious PowerShell command to the clipboard and instructed users to paste and run it, executing a VBScript credential harvester.
incidents.impact: Credential theft from Ukrainian government sector workers and diaspora employees in France, US, and Canada; access to organizational systems for intelligence collection on Ukrainian government operations abroad.

incidents.victim: Iraqi critical infrastructure (telecommunications and aviation sectors) and Israeli entities
incidents.vector: Blinder Tunnel campaign: spear-phishing via fake Dubai Airports recruitment lures deployed ShelbyLoader V2; GitHub repository API used as covert command-and-control channel; custom tunneling malware established persistent access.
incidents.impact: Initial access established in Iraqi telecommunications and aviation sectors; campaign extended to target an Israeli entity in May–June 2026. GitHub C2 infrastructure has been taken down; campaign active from at least November 2025 through June 2026.
